## Probability Both Balls Are Red

**Setup:** 3 red + 2 blue = 5 balls total. Two are drawn **without replacement**.

**Calculation:**

$$P(\text{both red}) = P(\text{1st is red}) \times P(\text{2nd is red} \mid \text{1st is red})$$

- First draw: $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of the balls are red.
- After removing one red, 2 red remain out of 4 total: $\dfrac{2}{4}$.

$$P(\text{both red}) = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{2}{4} = \frac{6}{20} = \frac{3}{10}$$

$$\boxed{\dfrac{3}{10}}$$

The user is asking for a probability problem. Let me work through it.

A box contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls, so 5 balls total.

Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are red?

P(both red) = P(first is red) × P(second is red | first is red)

P(first is red) = 3/5
P(second is red | first is red) = 2/4 = 1/2

P(both red) = (3/5) × (1/2) = 3/10

The fraction 3/10 is already in simplest form since gcd(3,10) = 1.
